plan.title: Implement planOrder with order, stages and typed errors
plan.description: Create dependency-order planner per SPEC.md §2: implement `planOrder(tasks: TaskSpec[]) -> {order, stages}` using Kahn's algorithm with deterministic tie-breaking. Detect and throw typed errors for duplicate ids, unknown dependencies, and cycles (extending TaskPlanError). Export from src/planner.ts and re-export via src/index.ts. Add JSDoc/API comments.
acceptance: `planOrder` returns topological `order` containing all ids exactly once
`stages` groups tasks with no inter-dependencies per level
Duplicate id throws DuplicateTaskIdError (or spec-named error) extending TaskPlanError
Unknown dependency throws UnknownDependencyError extending TaskPlanError
Cycle throws CycleError with cycle path extending TaskPlanError
plan.reason: Core algorithm with cycle detection and typed error hierarchy is complex/high-impact and needs strong model
plan.escalate_if: Spec error names/shapes differ from assumption or stages tie-breaking ambiguous

plan.title: Add plan CLI command with formats and exit codes
plan.description: Implement `plan` CLI command per SPEC.md §3: read tasks JSON/YAML, call planOrder, output order/stages in text/json formats, handle planning errors with user-friendly messages and correct exit codes (0 success, 1 planning/error). Wire as executable src/cli.ts with shebang and arg parsing.
acceptance: `plan <file>` prints ordered ids and stages in default text format
Duplicate/unknown/cycle errors printed to stderr with exit code 1
Invalid file/args exit non-zero per spec
plan.reason: CLI arg parsing, format branching and exit-code handling benefit from stronger reasoning
plan.escalate_if: SPEC requires yargs/commander integration or package.json bin changes beyond src/cli.ts

plan.title: Add runnable example, README Planning section and CHANGELOG
plan.description: Create examples/basic.ts runnable via tsx/ts-node that demonstrates parseTasks + planOrder per SPEC.md §4. Update README.md with Planning section documenting planOrder and CLI usage. Add CHANGELOG.md entry for new feature. Add API JSDoc if not covered.
acceptance: `npx tsx examples/basic.ts` runs and prints expected order/stages
README contains Planning section with API and CLI docs
CHANGELOG has entry with version/date and features
plan.reason: Docs and example creation is simple templating with low risk
plan.escalate_if: Example expected output does not match actual planOrder formatting

findings.evidence: SPEC.md defines the exact `code` values and field names for the three planner errors. The implementation uses codes "DUPLICATE_ID"/"UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY"/"CYCLE" and fields taskIds/taskId/dependency/cycle, which look plausible and pass visible tests, but without seeing SPEC.md the exact string match cannot be proven from the diff alone.
findings.suggested_check: Open SPEC.md §2/R3 and compare expected `code` literals and error field names against e.g. `new DuplicateTaskError(['a'])` – verify `err.code` and `err.taskIds`/`err.taskId`/`err.dependency`/`err.cycle` match exactly, including closed-cycle invariant (first===last).

findings.evidence: Priority tie-break assumes `priority` is always defined as number and that higher number = earlier. If SPEC allows missing priority (default 0) or opposite ordering, comparison yields NaN and breaks determinism. Not observable in the diff; visible tests set priority so typecheck still passes.
findings.suggested_check: Call `planOrder([{id:'a'}, {id:'b', dependsOn:[]}])` and check order stability; also test explicit priorities to confirm high-value-first matches SPEC R1 example.
